Definition: oh that!; with leave, or if it please
BiblicalUsage: Oh that, if it please, pray excuse me — this is the word for an entreaty, and it appears twelve times, always on the lips of someone asking for something hard. In Exodus 4:10 Moses says, O my Lord, I am not eloquent, and in Exodus 4:13 he says, O my Lord, send, I pray thee, by the hand of him whom thou wilt send. In Judges 6:15 Gideon says, Oh my Lord, wherewith shall I save Israel? And in 1 Kings 3:17 the woman before Solomon begins, O my lord, I and this woman dwell in one house.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this little word is the sound of honest prayer: not demanding, but pleading — and God answers pleading.
